subject: Throughput surge and elevated errors — executive brief, corrective backlog, and sign-off
messages:
From: Elaine Chang <elaine@rapidretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@rapidretail.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: High throughput tail & elevated 5xx rate impacting checkout - immediate exec review requested

Marcus —

We just hit a sustained throughput degradation starting ~08:50 PDT. Checkout latency tails are spiking (p95 -> 7s, p99 -> 18s) and we're seeing a jump in 500/502 errors across regions. This is impacting live checkouts and a handful of campaigns are failing to complete.

Our SRE team opened a bridge at 08:55 but the workarounds so far (traffic shifting, client-side retry increase) are short-lived. Given the revenue impact we're requesting an executive-level readout and a concrete remediation timeline. Can Redwood commit to a 48-hour action plan and a proposed credit/SLA accommodation?

I've looped procurement for any contractual follow-ups. Attaching a short CSV export with peak request IDs and timestamps for your diagnostics.

Attachments: rapidretail_peak_ids_20270512.csv (attachment stub)

Thanks,
Elaine Chang
Head of Platform Operations
RapidRetail

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Chang <elaine@rapidretail.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com, sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High throughput tail & elevated 5xx rate impacting checkout - immediate exec review requested

Elaine —

Thanks for the flag and for the data. I’m sorry for the impact here. We’ve spun up an incident bridge with infra and serving runtime leads (Karthik and Jordan cc’d). Immediate notes:

- We see matching error spikes in our telemetry; initial hypothesis is a cache pressure + kernel path regression during sustained long sequences causing amplification under bursty traffic.
- Priority: stabilize customer-facing traffic, then run targeted mitigations (LRU tuning + temporary routing to a compatible quantized model variant).

I’m scheduling an executive readout at 10:30 PDT and will send a short incident timeline. For transparency I attached the initial timeline export (throughput_timeline_v1.pdf).

Proposed immediate commitments:
- Stabilize within 4 hours (mitigation windows active)
- Full RCA and corrective backlog by EOD today
- 48-hour remediation sprint with daily check-ins and executive summary at 48h

Can you confirm a good contact for the executive readout? I’ll include our Head of Customer Success and our CTO on the bridge if you want executive parity.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Principal, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachment: throughput_timeline_v1.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Chang <elaine@rapidretail.com>, procurement@rapidretail.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com, sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Readout: Root causes, corrective backlog, and exec approvals required (RR-4872)

Elaine / RapidRetail team —

Follow-up from the 10:30am readout. Team verified the immediate mitigation reduced error rate by ~70% and trimmed p99 latency from 18s to 6s for affected routes. Below is a concise RCA and the corrective backlog requiring execution and exec approvals:

1) Immediate root causes (summary)- Cache churn: an LRU eviction storm caused frequent KV cache misses on hot prefixes under campaign bursts.- Kernel path regression: a recent micro-optimization for attention kernels increased tail latency on long sequences for the quantized path. Under heavy concurrent traffic this produced queuing that manifested as 500/502 errors.

2) Actions completed (during bridge)- Deployed temporary routing rules to divert critical checkout traffic to stable runtime variant.- Rolled back the kernel optimization on a small canary fleet.- Increased autoscaling headroom for affected GPU pools.

3) Corrective backlog (owner / ETA)
- Root-cause patch for kernel path (Karthik) — ETA: 72 hours for tested fix, 5 day rollout plan.
- Cache eviction tuning + workload-aware TTL (SRE) — ETA: 48 hours to push tuned config and validate.
- Automated prefix hot-key detection + pre-warming (Infra) — ETA: 14 days.
- Billing/SLA accommodation proposal (Customer Success + Finance) — Draft to Elaine by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: rr-4872-corrective_backlog.csv (scoped tasks and owners).

Approvals required from RapidRetail execs:
- Acceptance of the 72-hour kernel patch rollout with canary gating.
- Confirmation to proceed with temporary cost-bearing autoscaling increments while fixes are validated.
- Authorization to apply a one-time service credit if post-remediation performance does not meet the agreed SLOs for May 12 incident window.

Linking the triage ticket and workboard here: JIRA: RR-4872; Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/RR-4872-Throughput+Surge+Readout

Subject: Re: Readout: Root causes, corrective backlog, and exec approvals required (RR-4872)

Marcus —

Thanks for the clear summary and the quick mitigation. We accept the 72-hour kernel patch plan under the proposed canary gating. Procurement requests the SLA credit proposal in writing (line items please) and will review by COB Thursday.

We also request executive confirmation that Redwood will prioritize the cache pre-warm work (14-day item) — that work materially reduces our exposure for holiday campaigns. Please add your Head of CS and CTO on the follow-up summary so our execs can align signoff and any commercial remediation.

We’ll plan a 48-hour check-in at 09:30am PDT on Friday.

Elaine Chang
Head of Platform Operations
RapidRetail
